openings.claim: A hand-held broad resilient tapping face may spread force across the tile while repeated impulses move the adhesive bed, lowering height without concentrated edge loading.
openings.discriminator: Predicts fewer chips than a narrow face; any chip or persistent height mismatch defeats adequacy. Relative adjustment time is unspecified.
openings.probe: Proposed only: compare chips and height change against a narrow face on sacrificial matched beds; stop on any chip or persistent mismatch.
openings.uncertainty: Pad stiffness, bed-curing sensitivity, and tile/bed properties are unknown; safety is unproved.

openings.claim: Warming before tapping might change adhesive response and reduce required impulse, but its predicted advantage over broad-pad tapping depends on reversible warmth response.
openings.discriminator: No reduction in required impulse defeats the proposed advantage.
openings.probe: Only after explicit relaxation of no heating: compare warmed and ambient sacrificial beds for required impulse; no thermal source is supplied.
openings.uncertainty: Adhesive reversibility and resulting bond integrity are unknown; heating remains barred in this case.

lineage.reason: Preserves force distribution, impulse-driven movement, chip/mismatch gates and unknown stiffness/curing.
Preserves warmth-response dependency, impulse discriminator and explicit constraint-relaxation gate.

Frame-mounted sustained distributed force predicts gradual bed movement but violates hand-held use. Absence of impacts cannot establish chip safety; crack risk, load and precision remain unresolved. Surrogate cracking study would not establish in-case fit.

decision: Consider D1 for hypothetical sacrificial evaluation only. Enforce no edge chipping, hand-held adjustment and no adhesive heating. D2 requires changed authorization; reject fixed pressing. All proposals/predictions are synthetic, with no real tile, adhesive or equipment supplied and no observed effectiveness or safety.
